about: #4628: each surviving det-port mutant stated `equivalent` or `unreachable`, with the Java change and why it cannot alter observable behaviour; proposed in a PR, reviewed by the owner. A run that kills a stated mutant fails (the claim was wrong). Ids are mutation.py's; before / after are the Java line.

verdicts.equivalent: the change cannot alter anything the program shows (output, screen, files, COMMAREA, abend)
verdicts.unreachable: no input of the program reaches the changed code
verdicts.harness-gap: the change alters behaviour the proof runs but does not compare (open: the harness must)
verdicts.case-gap: an input the case lacks would kill it (open: strengthen the case)

survivors.reason: WS-VARIABLES' first byte is WS-PGMNAME, which the port keeps as a typed Java field (initialState sets it to 'COTRN02C'); the image byte is never read, and COTRN02C names no group item over WS-VARIABLES.

IMAGE of DFHCOMMAREA (a later chunk, byte offsets 3600 / 14700 / 19800 / 29400 of the 32767-byte image): COTRN02C reads DFHCOMMAREA only as DFHCOMMAREA(1:EIBCALEN) into the 218-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, which keeps at most the first 218 bytes, and in_ / the byte[] copy write those first; a byte this far in is never read, and for a terminal task the area's final contents are not observable (CICS discards them; linked_result drops them).

CSUTLDTC's LS-DATE / LS-DATE-FORMAT are LINKAGE items: handleCall moves the caller's 10-byte value over each in full before PROCEDURE DIVISION runs, so the initial image (run once, from the constructor) is never read.

performThru grows only at a PERFORM nesting depth of 64; CSUTLDTC nests at most 2 (MAIN, A000-MAIN THRU A000-MAIN-EXIT).

CSUTLDTC's PERFORM A000-MAIN THRU A000-MAIN-EXIT reaches the scan once, at depth 1 after A000-MAIN returns; performThru is [2, 2, 0, ...] (index 2 is never written), and none of the entries the `mine + 1` start adds (indexes 2 and 1) nor index 0 equals i = 1, so no PerformExit is thrown either way.

survivors.before: private final Field f89_TITLE02I = Field.alphanumeric(s_COTRN2AI, 107, 40, false);
survivors.after: private final Field f89_TITLE02I = Field.alphanumeric(s_COTRN2AI, 107, 41, false);
survivors.reason: TITLE02I as 41 bytes: COTRN02C never references TITLE02I; it is written only by RECEIVE's DetCics.typed when the terminal returns TITLE02, where the 41st byte (a space) lands on CURTIMEL's high byte (the O-side filler), which only SEND MAP's cursor test (CURTIMEL = -1) reads, and X'20..' is never -1.

survivors.after: private final Field f193_TRNNAMEO = Field.alphanumeric(s_COTRN2AI, 19, 5, false);
survivors.reason: TRNNAMEO as 5 bytes: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO's MOVE of the 4-byte WS-TRANID pads a 5th space, so the screen text is 'CT02 ' (the harness drops trailing blanks) and the byte after it (TITLE01L's high byte, O-side filler) holds X'20', which SEND MAP's cursor test (TITLE01L = -1) does not read as -1.

caWhole() restores the full DFHCOMMAREA array only for a stated commarea_length (none here); the shifted copy (destination offset 1, length < 32767) cannot throw, and the restored bytes are read only by fill_ into the task's COMMAREA object, which for a terminal task is not observable (linked_result drops it); the RETURN / XCTL COMMAREA is out_'s copy of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA.

DFHCOMMAREA's initial image: COTRN02C reads DFHCOMMAREA only as DFHCOMMAREA(1:EIBCALEN) (EIBCALEN = 0 takes the XCTL arm without reading it), and every byte of those EIBCALEN bytes was just written by in_ (all 218 bytes of the DTO) or the byte[] / link-area copy, so the image cannot show.
ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS belongs to ACCOUNT-RECORD (CVACT01Y), which COTRN02C COPYs but never references; its initial value cannot show.
handlers is written only by HANDLE CONDITION / HANDLE ABEND, which COTRN02C does not contain, so it is empty at the start of every task and clearing it does nothing.
COTRN02C never reads EIBDATE / EIBTIME (the header date and time come from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE through the task's clock; it references only EIBCALEN and EIBAID), and DFHEIBLK is not compared.

survivors.before: s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond = raw.length > keep ? java.util.Arrays.copyOfRange(raw, keep, raw.length) : null;
survivors.after: s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond = raw.length >= keep ? java.util.Arrays.copyOfRange(raw, keep, raw.length) : null;
survivors.reason: raw.length >= keep differs from > only at raw.length == 32767 (beyond becomes an empty array, not null, whose write-back copies 0 bytes), and a COMMAREA is at most 32763 bytes; the branch also runs only for a LINKed task.

survivors.before: caBack = () -> { typed.run(); System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.bytes, 0, raw, 0, Math.min(raw.length, keep)); if (s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond != null) { System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond, 0, raw, keep, raw.length - keep); } };
survivors.after: caBack = () -> { typed.run(); System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.bytes, 0, raw, 0, Math.min(raw.length, keep)); if (s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond != null) { System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond, 0, raw, keep, raw.length + keep); } };
survivors.reason: The `raw.length + keep` length sits inside `if (s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond != null)`, non-null only for a link area longer than the 32767-byte DFHCOMMAREA, which CICS cannot pass (COMMAREA is at most 32763 bytes).

survivors.before: caBack = () -> { typed.run(); System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.bytes, 0, raw, 0, Math.min(raw.length, keep)); if (s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond != null) { System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond, 0, raw, keep, raw.length - keep); } };
survivors.after: caBack = () -> { typed.run(); System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.bytes, 0, raw, 0, Math.min(raw.length, keep)); if (s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond == null) { System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond, 0, raw, keep, raw.length - keep); } };
survivors.reason: The link-area branch (task.linkArea() non-null) runs only for a LINKed task and this case is not linked (no scenario has an area); with `beyond` null the inverted test calls arraycopy on null (NullPointerException) at the RETURN. A sibling case with "linked": true (any ENTER scenario) would run the write-back and kill it.

With `||` every task cuts DFHCOMMAREA to EIBCALEN bytes; COTRN02C references DFHCOMMAREA only as (1:EIBCALEN), and in_ (before the cut) and fill_ (after caWhole restores the full array) see the whole array either way, so cutting or not cutting is unobservable.
`calen <= length` differs from `<` only at calen = 32767, a COMMAREA CICS cannot pass (at most 32763 bytes); there the 'cut' is a same-size copy that caWhole restores.

caBack = caWhole(whole); typed.run() only matters for a stated commarea_length (exactCommarea), and no scenario states one. Without the restore, the RETURN's caBack runs fill_ over the cut array and throws (-> PastFrom). Add add-by-account with "commarea_length": 100 (a SEND / RETURN ending).

The finally's caWhole(caWhole) restores the full DFHCOMMAREA array for a task that ends without caBack (XCTL, abend); only a stated commarea_length leaves it cut, and none does. Without the restore, the next scenario's initialState arraycopy of the 32767-byte image into the cut array throws. Add a PF3 scenario (XCTL) with "commarea_length": 100 followed by any other scenario (same service instance).

perform() reaches this scan only after a paragraph that is not its range's last returns; COTRN02C's PERFORMs each name one paragraph (from == thru) and MAIN-PARA (runTask's perform(0, 17)) always ends in RETURN / XCTL / an abend (Goback), so the scan over outer PERFORMs never runs.

MAIN-PARA's SET ERR-FLG-OFF TO TRUE stores 'N'; the program tests only ERR-FLG-ON ('Y') (IF ERR-FLG-ON, IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON) and never ERR-FLG-OFF, and WS-ERR-FLG is not otherwise shown, so 'X' behaves as 'N'.

This is the RETURN at the end of MAIN-PARA: every branch before it ends in SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN (which ends with its own EXEC CICS RETURN) or in RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN's XCTL (transfers or abends), so control never reaches it.

SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN ends with EXEC CICS RETURN, so every statement that sets WS-ERR-FLG to 'Y' is followed, through PERFORM SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN, by the end of the task: this 'X' (for 'Y') is never tested

VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS' IF ERR-FLG-ON is never true there: WS-ERR-FLG is 'N' at task start and every statement that sets it 'Y' is followed by PERFORM SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN, whose EXEC CICS RETURN ends the task.
PERFORM SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN THRU RECEIVE-TRNADD-SCREEN: SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN ends with EXEC CICS RETURN, so the range end is never reached

survivors.before: f18_WS_TRAN_AMT_N = Cobol.zoned(Hfp.fixedStore(v3, 2, false), 11, 2, true, false, CS);
survivors.after: f18_WS_TRAN_AMT_N = Cobol.zoned(Hfp.fixedStore(v3, 2, false), 12, 2, true, false, CS);
survivors.reason: WS-TRAN-AMT-N is S9(9)V99; after the format check (sign, 8 digits, '.', 2 digits) |NUMVAL-C(TRNAMTI)| < 10^8, so neither the 11-digit nor a 12-digit store truncates anything.

RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN's IF CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM = LOW-VALUES OR SPACES is never true: both callers set CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM first ('COSGN00C', 'COMEN01C', or CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM when that is neither SPACES nor LOW-VALUES), so the MOVE 'COSGN00C' never runs and `&&` (never true for one field) is the same.

The failed-XCTL test in RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN (no RESP, so a failure goes through condition()): flipped, a failed XCTL skips condition() and falls through to the final RETURN instead of abending. No scenario fails the XCTL. Add PF3 with fault {cmd XCTL, program COMEN01C, resp PGMIDERR} (abend AEI0).

condition() returns a value only for a handled, ignored (EOC) or ERROR-handled condition; COTRN02C sets no handler and a failed XCTL / ENDBR raises none ignored by default, so condition() throws (the abend) and `to` is never tested; the SEND MAP copy of the test (line 1593) sits in `if (0 != 0)` (no RESP, response constant 0).

RECEIVE MAP's zero fill of COTRN2AI only changes fields the terminal did not return, from the image's spaces / X'00' to X'00': COTRN02C tests an input field only against SPACES and / or LOW-VALUES (same branch for both), every unreturned length / attribute / colour / highlight byte is 0 or a space (not 'set' for DetCics.subfields, never -1), and the screen text compare drops trailing blanks and X'00'.

EIBRESP / EIBRESP2 are only stored by the translator after each command (RESP / RESP2 operands feed WS-RESP-CD / WS-REAS-CD directly from the command result); COTRN02C never references the EIB fields, so a missing store is never read, and DFHEIBLK is not compared.
